messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: alert - streaming-decode-service p99 6.2s (threshold 2.0s) across us-west-2. Multiple instances reporting paging/kernel evictions. Auto-escalation to eng-sre.
oncall-sre: seeing it on dashboards too. p95 ~1.1s, p99 trending way up. Any recent infra changes?
alice: pushed a small TRT8 + flashattn variant to canary last night (compilepath v2.4.1). Canary traffic at 3% across us-west-2. Not aware of kernel changes.
ben: looking at node logs now — lots of kernel messages: `mm: pagecache_reclaim hugepages?`, `compilepath: evicting kvcache`, `NVM: page fault 0xdeadbeef`. grabbing dmesg...
carla: also correlate with streaming tail tasks — queue depth for decode workers jumped 4x. KV cache hits dropped from 92% -> 35% around deploy time.
ben: paste of dmesg excerpt:
```
[6141592998.123] compilepath: eviction triggered for model=redwood-v1-kv size=1.2GB
[6141593001.451] flash_attn: fallback to generic kernel on SM mismatch
[6141593003.777] decode: pagefault on GPU0 -> host fallback
[6141593004.002] slab: hugepage reuse failed
```

sam: interesting — flashattn fallback log + compilepath eviction suggests a kernel/runtime mismatch. Which nodes got the new driver/kernel?
runtime-eng: we rolled a micro-update to cuda-driver and kernel-rt on a subset of hosts in us-west-2 at 23:52 UTC (maintenance window). It touched the canary pool.
oncall-sre: so two moving parts: TRT/FlashAttn variant and kernel/driver micro-update. Which one is the likely culprit?
alice: locally the model compiled fine, but real traffic exercises different seq lengths and KV cache patterns. TRTexec had an updated kernel flag `--enable-fused-kernel` in the build. Could be producing non-reentrant kernels under certain page pressure.
ben: perf snapshot from affected instance:
```
PID 12345 decode_worker
p95 latency 6.0s
syscalls showing heavy page reclaim, context-switch spikes
stack: compilepath_prepare -> flash_attn_init -> cuLaunchKernel -> page_fault_handler
```

ml-infra: customer-facing routing: we can reroute canary -> stable pool in 2 mins. Recommend to shift traffic off canary and scale stable nodes.
product-ops: any active customers affected? We've received 2 SEV tickets for degraded streaming performance from an enterprise account.
oncall-sre: immediate mitigations proposal: 1) reroute canary traffic to stable 2) scale up stable capacity + throttling for low-priority tenants 3) roll back kernel-driver micro-update on canary hosts 4) pause TRT8/flashattn variant rollout. Thoughts?
carla: agree. Also enable KV-cache warmup for stable to reduce cold miss storm. We should avoid node restart if possible.
ben: rollback plan for kernel-driver: we can toggle kernel package to previous build via orchestration `pkgctl rollback kernel-rt-5.18.3 -> 5.18.2` and trigger live-reload on a small batch. That should remove the flashattn fallback path.
runtime-eng: warning — rollback touches driver ABI; need to ensure CUDA driver compatibility. I'll run a quick compatibility check.
alice: pause rollout now. `deployctl pause rollout redwood/flashattn-trt8 --by=canary` (done).
ml-infra: rerouting canary traffic now -> stable (traffic shift 3% -> 0%). Monitoring ingress.
incident-bot: change: canary traffic rerouted by ml-infra at 6141593105.
carla: KV hit rate on stable after warmup: 88% -> small improvement. p99 dropping to ~2.5s but still above target.
ben: started kernel rollback to batch-1 hosts at 6141593300. Will update when batch completes.
product-ops: opened incident-XXXX for customer comms: note degraded streaming latency; ETA for mitigation ~30-45m.
ben: batch-1 rollback complete on 6/6 hosts. Observed p99 from those hosts improved to 1.9s. Aggregate p99 still 2.3s because some hosts remain with new kernel.
sam: start draining remaining canary hosts from load balancer and schedule rollback.
runtime-eng: compatibility check ok for rollback on remaining hosts. Proceeding.
oncall-sre: good. Keep a close eye on page fault metrics and KV eviction events. If p99 doesn't normalize after rollback, we may need a full model variant rollback (disable fused-kernel compile flag).
alice: preparing a hotfix build that sets `--enable-fused-kernel=false` and forces non-fused path. Build ready, will hold until we see full kernel rollback effect.
carla: after second batch rollback, p99 stable ~1.5s and streaming stalls reduced. Some residual tail events remain in a small subset of nodes due to eviction thrash.
ben: cleaned up kernel OOM/eviction counters on hosts; patched compilepath to avoid large immediate KV eviction on cold start (`eviction_threshold=0.85 -> 0.95`).
ml-infra: traffic gradually returned to normal pools; global p99 now 1.4s, p95 0.9s.
product-ops: customer update: informed of mitigation and that a detailed postmortem will follow. :white_check_mark:
oncall-sre: assigning follow-ups: - runtime-eng to collate kernel/driver changes and schedule safer rollout gating (runtime-eng) - alice + eng-ml to validate fused-kernel behavior across seq distributions (alice) - eng-sre to add alert for KV-hit drop delta >20% (ben) - product-ops to coordinate proactive comms with affected customers (product-ops).
runtime-eng: ack, will prepare stricter canary checks and add a preflight matrix: kernel version x driver variant x TRT build.
alice: will run end-to-end load tests with seq lengths 8, 32, 1024 and cold cache patterns.
oncall-sre: handoff to next oncall in 30m. Summary for pager: cause = interaction between kernel/driver micro-update + new TRT/flashattn fused kernel path causing increased pagefaults and compilepath KV evictions under production workload; mitigation = pause rollout, reroute canary traffic, rollback kernel-driver on affected hosts, patch compile flags and eviction thresholds. Current status = service stable, p99 within SLO but monitoring for regressions.
oncall-sre: @oncall-next you are up next. full thread: incident bot alerts + mitigation steps recorded above.
oncall-sre: closing active incident channel for now; creating postmortem draft ticket INC-zh-2026-001.
product-ops: thanks team. quick debrief on postmortem: include customer impact window, timeline of deploys, metrics snapshots, and recommended gating matrix.
ben: adding logs + dmesg excerpts to the postmortem ticket.
incident-bot: incident INC-zh-2026-001 created at 6141600180.
oncall-sre: thumbs up. handing off. :v:
